node-1.label: A man in his 40s presented with 4 months of progressive leg paresthesias and subjective leg weakness

why.why: The unremarkable neurological examination supports a functional etiology, and the symptoms are subjective. Expert analysis states that functional disorder cannot be fully excluded while confirmatory organic workup is pending, so it remains a relevant consideration at the same confidence.

A normal exam does not exclude early or small-fiber neuropathy, and progressive subjective symptoms are consistent. Expert analysis agrees peripheral neuropathy is the leading explanation but notes that confirmatory NCS/EMG, metabolic labs, and skin biopsy results are pending, so it remains unconfirmed; confidence is therefore increased from 0.35 to 0.4.

Metabolic deficiencies can present with a normal exam early in the course, and progression warrants laboratory workup. Expert analysis notes metabolic causes cannot be fully excluded and that metabolic labs are pending, so confidence remains moderate-low at 0.25.

The Pathologist explicitly states that a spinal cord lesion has been ruled out (脊髓病变已被否定), and the unremarkable neurological examination provides no upper motor neuron or myelopathic signs. This expert analysis strengthens the prior refutation, so confidence in a spinal cord lesion is reduced from 0.1 to 0.05.

node-7.label: Confirmatory workup (NCS/EMG, metabolic labs, skin biopsy, detailed history) has been requested but results are not yet available

why.why: The Pathologist's explicit suspicion of small-fiber neuropathy supports this earlier hypothesis. The normal examination does not exclude small-fiber involvement, and the pending OGTT/HbA1c and serologic/genetic panels will help exclude metabolic or immune causes. Confidence increases from 0.25 to 0.30, but remains moderate because objective test results are still awaited.

node-9.label: Quantitative sensory testing and autonomic assessment have been identified as part of the diagnostic workup to differentiate functional disease, but results are not yet available

why.why: The Pathologist explicitly suspects small-fiber neuropathy given the normal neurological examination and progressive leg paresthesias with subjective weakness. This direct expert endorsement raises confidence in small-fiber neuropathy. However, confirmatory tests—including skin biopsy, NCS/EMG, OGTT/HbA1c, and serologic/genetic panels—are still pending, so the diagnosis remains unconfirmed; confidence is therefore increased modestly from 0.35 to 0.40.

node-11.label: Metabolic/toxic neuropathy (e.g., B12 deficiency, diabetic neuropathy)

attrs.why: Metabolic deficiency (node-5) is a relevant hypothesis in the belief, and metabolic labs are still pending (node-7). A normal early neurological examination with progressive paresthesias and subjective weakness is compatible with a metabolic or toxic cause of peripheral neuropathy, making this a meaningful etiologic refinement of the current frontier.

CIDP is an immune-mediated peripheral neuropathy that can present with progressive leg paresthesias and subjective weakness. Although the unremarkable examination and lack of reflex/electrophysiologic data make it less likely, pending NCS/EMG results (node-7) are essential to differentiate this subtype from other peripheral neuropathies.
